text: On the twenty-eighth of April, 2021, a spacecraft called Parker Solar Probe flew into the Sun's atmosphere.
It stayed inside for about five hours, thirteen million kilometres above the Sun's visible surface.
The visible surface is about five and a half thousand degrees Celsius. The atmosphere above it, the corona, reaches up to two million.
That's hundreds of times hotter than the surface.
Behind its heat shield, the instruments stayed at a cosy eighty-five degrees Fahrenheit. That's about thirty Celsius.
A warm day, inside the Sun's own atmosphere.
So how did it stay that cool? The full video on our channel has the answer. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
